tools.name: Exact neighborhood-type quotient upper construction
tools.abstraction: Partition each bipartite side by exact complement-neighborhood equality. When the class maps are surjective and adjacency is constant on class products, type-class graph rectangles and the registered quotient lift give rho(G)<=D_intersection(G)<=min(t_row,t_column).
preconditions: finite bipartite associated graph with exact full complement neighborhoods
surjective nonempty row and column type classes
adjacency constant on every class product
registered quotient/type-class cover upper-bound direction applies
structural_signature: many ambient vertices share identical complement stars
target quantity admits a cover lifted from exact quotient classes
small min(row types,column types) can falsify superlogarithmic growth at the tested level
tools.operation: prove exact row and column neighborhood equivalence classes, form the quotient, then lift the smaller type-class rectangle cover or an explicit quotient cover
guaranteed_effects: a proved type classification yields the finite upper bound rho(G)<=min(t_row,t_column)
an explicit smaller quotient cover can improve that finite upper bound
non_guarantees: does not give a lower bound
does not bound later levels without a uniform type-growth theorem
does not imply recurrence, circuit lower bounds, novelty or P versus NP
worked at G9/G13 does not mean every encoded family stays quotient-cheap
validation_obligations: prove full neighborhood equality rather than sample equality
account for accumulated old bands and fallback edges
check both row and column types
preserve complement/associated-graph polarity and quotient-lift assumptions
proof_backing: C042 explicit type-class and two-pair proofs
